steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you really have something to do with the radio station... then...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Do you know about the urban legends about "Ghost Calls" and this radio station?
You seemed to have frightened Eleven. Her shoulders hunch up and her head slowly lowers...

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "I... I don't know... After I arrived in this world, I lost my voice..."

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "If... the owner of this record store hadn't remembered me... I..."
Eleven glances towards the store entrance. The store owner is dozing off in her chair, her phonograph head bobbing up and down, her stylus flicking.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We were drawn into this by the legend of the "Ghost Calls" and a radio show called "Call at 3 AM" The record you played for us is a recording of that show, which makes me suspicious of you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Can you tell me why you lost your voice? Nino and I have faced similar dangers, but we didn't lose our voices.
Eleven picks up her comms device, seemingly wanting to type something, but in the end, she stops. Other than shaking her head, she makes no other movements.

options: You are inextricably linked to the "radio station" that controls this world.
Does your phone have anything to do with you losing your voice?

steps.content: Your voice becomes a little high-pitched from urgency, which makes Eleven lower her head even more. She bites her lip, unable to utter even simple syllables, only shaking her head.

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: You're so scary... Even if it's for work, can't you be a bit gentler with ladies?

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: ...What are you staring at me for?
The store owner, who had been sitting at the doorway, also comes over after hearing the commotion. She gently squeezes Eleven's shoulder and speaks to you in a somewhat humble tone.

steps.speaker: Record Store Owner
steps.content: Oh officer, she loves those pleasant sounds, so she mimicked the radio show host and recorded quite a few opening lines. But now that she can't speak anymore, she's more anxious than anyone else.

steps.speaker: Record Store Owner
steps.content: Whenever that radio show at 3 a.m. starts, Eleven can't sleep... Look at the dark circles under her eyes. They're practically all the way down to her chin...
Eleven hurriedly nods. She sneaks a glance at you, then lowers her eyes, not daring to meet your gaze.
Seeing this situation, you sigh softly, then squat down to look directly into Eleven's eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to scare you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is a serious issue with a big impact. I'm guessing that many people in the real world have also been implicated. So... if you know the "Radio Ghost" who's causing the trouble, you should try to give me some clues.
Eleven lowers her eyes and bites her lips. Her low spirits are almost palpable.
She lightly taps her comms device, typing rapidly.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "If I did something wrong, please just tell me. If my performance is poor, or if I made you uncomfortable, it's all my fault..."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm not blaming you. I just want... to find a solution as soon as possible.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You also want to get your voice back, right?
Eleven thinks for a moment, then starts typing slowly.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "I've always loved radio shows. After graduating from college, with the encouragement of the owner of this record store, I got an offer from a radio station and was about to have my own program."

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "But... because I was inexperienced and new, they kept pushing back the time slot they gave me, until finally I got a 3 a.m. program..."

Eleven didn't finish typing, but you both could guess what happened next. Entering the workplace as someone with no experience or background, she'd have to endure all the bullying and unfair treatment.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I'm sorry. It was my fault just now. I was stressed from overworking.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Next time I do something rude, please stop me immediately.
You calm down, sigh, and apologize to Eleven.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: How terrible. Why not try to fight back? It's infuriating just hearing about it!
Eleven shakes her head vigorously, and quickly types a few lines on the comms device.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: "No, no... that won't do. I... I don't know anything, and I can't do anything right. How can I question others' arrangements? They... they must have their reasons for doing this..."
The words on the device are a bit glaring. You remember hearing it somewhere.
The radio station here, and those... strange people on the streets.
Ha. I was wondering why a record store would have such terrible noises...
So it's a bunch of untransformed freaks, eh?
Hey, stop making those awful sounds. Either shut up or become a normal person!
